author: Joshua Fluke
description:
HR tells employees to speak up, be honest, use the open-door policy, complete anonymous surveys and trust that conversations will be handled confidentially.

But HR works for the company.

That changes what all of those things actually mean.

In this video, we’re going through what HR is really doing when employees complain, why managers suddenly start documenting everything, how performance improvement plans can become paper trails, what “confidentiality” actually means at work, why anonymous employee surveys may reveal more than employees realize, what exit interviews are really used for, and why HR often acts as the buffer between executives and employees.

You can work somewhere for years with good reviews and suddenly every conversation becomes an email.

Every tiny mistake becomes a formal issue.

Goals suddenly become hyper-specific.

Your manager starts writing messages like they’re preparing evidence for court.

Then comes the performance improvement plan.

title: HOW HR LEGALLY LIES TO EMPLOYEES
